html:
German South West Africa was the German colony in what is now Namibia, begun in 1884 when Germany placed under its protection the land around Lüderitz Bay bought by the Bremen merchant Adolf Lüderitz.

It was Germany's only true settler colony. Officials played Herero and Nama leaders against each other, and settlers took cattle and land. After the risings of 1904 the army carried out the Herero and Nama genocide, and the survivors were forced into labour. Diamonds were found near Lüderitz in 1908, and Kolmanskop boomed.

South African troops conquered it in 1915 during the First World War. German place names, buildings in Windhoek and Swakopmund and a German-speaking minority remain, and Germany's apology and aid talks with Namibia still continue.
sum: German South West Africa was the German colony in what is now Namibia, begun in 1884 when Germany placed under its protection the land around Lüderitz Bay bought by the Bremen merchant Adolf Lüderitz.
